newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees at least two rivals to France Telecom.
newsitem.headline: France sees at least two rivals to France Telecom.

text.p: The head of French telecoms regulator ART said in an interview published on Monday that he expected a second rival to emerge for France Telecom SA in addition to Generale des Eaux unit Cegetel, but probably not as early as January 1998.
"It is likely that on January 1, 1998, there will be only one operator competing on all fronts against France Telecom, Cegetel," Jean-Michel Hubert told the newspaper Les Echos.
Cegetel is a unit of Generale des Eaux and counts British Telecommunications Plc, Mannesmann AG and SBC Communications Inc among its investors.

"But competition presupposes the opening of the market to more than two players. Our legal and pricing structures allow that. It demands a large financial capacity on the part of the candidates in a market where investments are counted in billions (of francs)," he said.

"I presume that the creation of a third all-round operator will imply the formation of alliances. But it is not up to ART to render judgment on an alliance. We only have to define the conditions for effective and loyal competition," Hubert said.
He said ART would render a decision concerning access to Internet via cable television networks before the end of June.
